subject: english
title: Roots: Work, Write, Quick
objective: Identify the base words work, write, and quick in common related words.
introduction: Milo worked on a note, wrote his name, and moved quickly to class. Can you find each base word?

vocabulary.definition: to do a job or task that needs effort
to make letters or words with a pencil or pen
happening in a short amount of time

activities.instruction: Read the pair and find the word that carries the main meaning.
activities.content: A root or base word carries the central meaning. Word endings can change how the word is used.

feedback.retry: Read both words again and find the part that stays the same.

activities.prompt: Learn how a base word stays inside a related word.
activities.narration: A base word carries the main meaning. An ending can change the word’s job or time.
activities.guideHint: Read both words and look for the part that stays the same.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: A base word carries the main meaning. An ending can change the word’s job or time.

activities.instruction: Tap each pair that keeps the same base word.

feedback.retry: Look for the letters that stay the same.

activities.prompt: Find pairs with a shared base word.
activities.narration: In a related pair, the base-word letters stay while an ending is added.
activities.guideHint: Compare the letters at the beginning of both words.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: In a related pair, the base-word letters stay while an ending is added.

activities.instruction: Sort pairs that share a base word from unrelated pairs.

feedback.retry: Find the word part that stays before sorting again.

activities.prompt: Sort each pair by whether one word grows from the other.
activities.narration: A word family shares a base word; an unrelated pair has no word part that carries both meanings.
activities.guideHint: Check whether one word keeps the main word part from the other.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: A word family shares a base word; an unrelated pair has no word part that carries both meanings.

activities.instruction: Tap the pair that shares a base word.

feedback.retry: Check which pair shares the same base-word letters.

activities.prompt: Choose the pair with one word grown from the other.
activities.narration: A shared base word keeps its letters when an ending is added.
activities.guideHint: Look for one word inside the other without its ending.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: A shared base word keeps its letters when an ending is added.

activities.instruction: Match each pair to the ending rule it shows.

pairs.right: add -ed to show a past action
add -er to name a person who writes
add -ly to tell how an action happens

feedback.retry: Check the ending rule and the letters that stay.

activities.prompt: Match each word pair with the rule that explains its connection.
activities.narration: The ending tells what changed, while the base word keeps the central meaning.
activities.guideHint: Read the ending and ask what it tells about the word.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: The ending tells what changed, while the base word keeps the central meaning.

activities.instruction: Put the base-word steps in order.

feedback.retry: Check that you read, compared, noticed, and named the base word.

activities.prompt: Order the steps for finding a base word.
activities.narration: Compare the letters that stay before naming the base word.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Compare the letters that stay before naming the base word.

items.prompt: Milo worked on a class project. Which pair shows a base word and a related word?
items.explanation: Work is the base word, and -ed changes it to worked for a past action.

items.prompt: After removing -ed from 'worked,' which base word remains?
items.explanation: Removing -ed leaves work, the part that carries the main meaning.

items.prompt: Which word is made by adding -ed to 'work'?
items.explanation: Adding -ed to work makes worked; the ending shows a past action.

items.prompt: Which pair is NOT a word family?
items.explanation: Cat and dog name two animals, but neither grows from the other. The other pairs share a base word.

items.prompt: What is the base word in 'writer'?
items.explanation: The letters write stay when -er is added, so write is the base word.
